|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-time-t0"></span>`time.t0` | string | | `2027-03-04T07:00:00Z` | | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The civil instant `SimTime` zero corresponds to, RFC 3339. It is what the 1609.2 `generationTime` is stamped from, and it is *scenario data*, not a wall-clock read. |
| <span id="s-time-duration-s"></span>`time.duration_s` | number | s | `60.0` | (0, ∞)<br>recommended 1 to 15 minutes to watch; 1 hour or more as a batch run. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How long the run lasts, simulated seconds. How much simulated time the run covers. A vehicle changes its pseudonym about every 5 minutes (SAE J2945/1), so privacy and credential studies need longer runs than radio studies. |
| <span id="s-time-mobility-step-ms"></span>`time.mobility_step_ms` | integer | ms | `100` | [10, 100] | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The mobility period, milliseconds, 10–100. |
| <span id="s-time-des-resolution"></span>`time.des_resolution` | string | | `1us` | `1ns`, `1us`, `1ms` | advanced | :material-filter-check:{ title="Only its implemented values load" } `refused` | The resolution models are promised, e.g. `1us`. The kernel is always nanoseconds; this is the guarantee a model may rely on. *Status: The resolution the run promises its models. The kernel keeps nanoseconds whatever this says; the loader refuses a resolution the run cannot keep — '1ms' with a PHY or MAC that times frames in microseconds, or a time-dilation window off the promised grid.* |
| <span id="s-time-metric-period-s"></span>`time.metric_period_s` | number | s | | [0.1, 3600] | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How often every metric provider flushes a window into a `metric.sample`, simulated seconds; 1 s when left out. A run of days at a minute's period writes a sixtieth of the samples — the long-run option that keeps `metrics.json` and the page's series a usable size — and each sample then summarises a minute instead of a second. Left out of the serialised scenario when not set, so no existing scenario's hash moves. |
| <span id="s-time-warmup-s"></span>`time.warmup_s` | number | s | | [0, ∞)<br>recommended 10 to 20 % of the run; 30 to 60 s on a city extract. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The warm-up period, simulated seconds: how long the run fills with traffic before it is measured. No metric sample is recorded for a window that ends inside it, so the charts and the metric summaries describe the steady state rather than an empty map filling up (the transient-deletion practice of Law, *Simulation Modeling and Analysis*, 5th ed., §9.5.1). The run report's whole-run counters still include it. Unset is none. How long the run fills with traffic before it is measured: charts and metric summaries skip it, so an empty map filling up does not drag the averages down. |
| <span id="s-time-calendar"></span>`time.calendar` | string | | | `real`, `compressed` | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Which calendar the credential system runs on. `real`, the default, is the deployment's: one-week i-periods counted from the US epoch, 2015-01-06 04:00 Eastern ([SMP] §2.1.17 Table 2), so a run starting 2026-10-16 provisions i = 614. `compressed` is the only way to state a shorter `security.protocol.params.i_period_s`: its i-period numbers, validity windows and every calendar-driven wait are not the deployment's, and the manifest and the run report say so. Left out of the serialised scenario when real, so no existing scenario's hash moves. |

## Choices

The labelled values of every closed or model setting above.

??? note "`time.des_resolution`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `1ns` | 1 nanosecond | The finest promise; models that time frames in microseconds are content. |
 | `1us` | 1 microsecond | What the radio models time frames in. The usual choice. |
 | `1ms` | 1 millisecond | Only for runs without a frame-level radio; refused with a medium or high PHY or MAC. |

??? note "`time.calendar`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `real` | Real | The deployment's weekly grid from the 2015 epoch. |
 | `compressed` | Compressed | A shorter i-period, labelled in every output. |
